title: Neymar records assist on return from left knee injury in 6-0 Santos win
content:
Former Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain star Neymar made his return from injury on Sunday by recording an assist in a 6-0 win over Velo Clube.

The Brazil international, playing his first game since undergoing arthroscopy surgery on his left knee, came on as a substitute at half-time and was subject to a late sliding challenge in the 78th minute from Velo Clube defender Islan that appeared to leave him in considerable pain.

Islan was booked for the tackle and Neymar recovered to set up Gabriel Barbosa’s goal three minutes later, Santos’ fifth on the night. The victory moved Santos up to eighth in the Campeonato Paulista, the top tier of football in the Brazilian state of Sao Paulo.

Neymar returned to Santos, where he began his career and came through the academy, in January 2025 after leaving Saudi Pro League team Al Hilal by mutual consent. He dealt with a hamstring issue for much of last year before battling through a knee injury to help Santos avoid relegation from Brazil’s Serie A, before eventually having surgery.

The 34-year-old is Brazil’s all-time leading scorer with 79 goals and has been capped 128 times, though he has not played for the nation since October 2023, when he ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee in a 2-0 defeat against Uruguay.

Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti said in September that he would have “no problems” selecting Neymar for his World Cup squad if he was fit to feature, with Santos head coach Juan Pablo Vojvoda emphasising Neymar’s importance at club and international level after the win on Sunday.

“I think everyone needs Neymar,” said Vojvoda, per Globo. “Santos, the national team…Ancelotti will be happy if he’s doing well. One thing will lead to another. He’s a world-class player.

“He still has that ambition. I see it in every little game, in every small-sided game in training, he wants to be there and he wants to win. That’s what motivates him.”

Neymar has made 29 appearances in his second spell at Santos, registering 11 goals and five assists. He extended his contract with the club in January, keeping him with the side until December 2026.

Brazil will play Morocco, Haiti and Scotland in Group C at the World Cup this summer.
